text.p: China's eastern metropolis of Shanghai has executed a man arrested for a recent series of killings, robberies and attacks on women that had alarmed the city, state television said on Friday.
Wei Guangxiu, 26, from nearby Anhui province was arrested in April and charged in a string of 13 attacks on women in which two died and 12 were injured, six seriously.
The Shanghai Second Intermediate Court had sentenced Wei to death on May 29, and the sentence was carried out on Friday, television said.
Wei had used an iron bar to batter his victims and then robbed them of cash and valuables worth 7,500 yuan ($903), the report said.
"The results of his crimes were extremely serious and the circumstances extremely evil," it said.
Rumours about the attacks swept the city and dominated conversations among Shanghai's 13 million people for more than a week before Wei's arrest.
